Utility

Switch the capacity network shown + searched. Substations, uploads, sites, footprint and save/load work across both. ComEd = kW corridors; Ameren = MW feeders.

Network

Re-shades ComEd corridors by the selected metric; Ameren switches its published generation/load tiles. “Combined” = the average of a feeder’s generation & load hosting capacity (ComEd corridors); Ameren shows generation.

Capacity legend (MW)

One MW scale for both utilities — ComEd corridors and Ameren’s published grid shading share the same bands and colors.

Dual-use eligibility
A site qualifies when a feeder meeting your generation and/or load minimums lies within the eligibility distance (one point of interconnection). The matched feeder ID is shown in each site’s breakdown.
Site eligibility (optional)
Substation & transmission criteria are optional — leave blank to not require them. Nearest distances are always computed & exported.

Substations

Tick the box above, then click a substation marker on the map to see its details.
Classification
0 shows all. A higher value hides substations below it (and those with unknown voltage).
Click a substation marker on the map to see its details.
Substations come from HIFLD plus OpenStreetMap, merged and de-duplicated by location, within the active service territory and colored by classification. Voltage is from HIFLD MAX_VOLT / OSM tags (blank = unknown, never treated as 0).

Planned grid investments

Utility investments filed with the Illinois Commerce Commission — where future capacity is likely to appear. These are not existing assets and are not reflected in either utility’s published hosting capacity.
Status
Most projects are named only by town, so the ring shows where the asset could be — not a precise site. Ring size reflects how well the location is actually known.
Tick the box above to load planned investments.
Sources: ComEd Docket 26-0047 and Ameren Illinois Docket 26-0051 (2028–2031 grid plans, both pending — ICC order due 15 Dec 2026), plus approved work in ComEd 22-0486 and Ameren 22-0487. Costs and headroom are as filed; headroom for ComEd conversions uses ComEd’s own published factors (+8 MW per new 12 kV circuit, +4 MW per 4→12 kV conversion).

Transmission lines

HIFLD transmission lines (all utilities) in the current view, colored by voltage class. Click a line for details.

Candidate Sites

Schools are the demand-side site universe \u2014 large, distributed, already-served parcels. The preview shows all Illinois NCES school locations; the button loads in-territory schools as analyzable candidate sites (Site analysis + Footprint).

Context (informational)

Equity / R3 + EJ communities
Illinois Equity Investment Eligible Communities (R3 + Environmental-Justice areas under CEJA) \u2014 where clean-energy & battery-storage equity incentives apply. Shown for context; not used in site matching.
Industrial parcels
CMAP Land Use Inventory (industrial / manufacturing / warehousing) across the 7-county region \u2014 Cook + DuPage, Kane, Kendall, Lake, McHenry, Will. Loads when zoomed in past ~metro scale.

Basemap

Use the imagery toggle at the bottom-left of the map to switch to satellite.

Upload sites

Excel/CSV needs lat, lon (or latitude, longitude). Each sheet becomes its own colored layer. Rows without coordinates are geocoded by address; points outside the territory are skipped.

Site analysis

Press Run Find (Find tab) to analyze every loaded site against the current parameters — it highlights matching feeders and analyzes the sites in one step. Each site shows feeders + sum gen/load within 0.1/0.3/0.5 mi, qualifying feeders, nearest substation & transmission line. With criteria set, only matching sites are listed (click chips to zoom).
Upload site files above, then click “Run Find”.

Add a site

Add your own sites — by clicking the map, by the address in the Find address box, or at your current location. Each is analyzed like an uploaded site. Saved in your browser; export anytime.

Site footprint

For each uploaded or manual site (all of them by default; tick the box below to restrict to Find matches), this pulls parcel + building footprint geometry to compute building area, lot area (geometry-computed and the assessor's recorded land sq ft), and outdoor area (lot − building) — all in ft². Building area comes from the national USA Structures layer (works anywhere). Lot/parcel data is pulled from county GIS for verified counties: Macon, Peoria, McLean, Madison, St. Clair, Vermilion, Adams, Coles, Morgan, Greene, Scott, Hancock, Henderson, McDonough, Jackson, Monroe. Some county servers refuse a browser request from a file opened directly; those rows fall back to building-only and say so. Elsewhere lot data isn't public, so only building area shows. Tip: run the dashboard through the Ameren_Server cell to unlock county data the browser otherwise blocks and to fill vendor-locked counties via ReportAllUSA.
All loaded sites
Load schools first (Layers → “Load in-territory schools”), then run this to footprint every school at once.
Set Find params + click Run Find (or add a manual site), then “Analyze footprint.”
Outdoor area = computed lot area − building footprint. A blank assessor column means the county record had no land-sqft field; the geometry-computed lot is the reliable figure. Multi-parcel sites are summed automatically.
Single point
Capture a point with Coordinate capture (Sites tab), then analyze it here — parcel area, building footprint, owner, and outdoor area.

Save / Load Session

Save filter settings, the radius center, uploaded layers, and your manual sites to a .json file, then load it back later. Or save a standalone .html copy of the whole map (data embedded) that opens offline from any folder.
